original_question: Let n >= 3, let Omega be an open subset of R^n, and let f: Omega -> R^n be a piecewise affine homeomorphism. Can f be approximated by diffeomorphisms in the Sobolev norm?
target_in_paper: Section 1, Proposition 1.2, read in the context of Conjecture 1.1 and Theorem 1.3: the reduced higher-dimensional Ball-Evans subproblem asking whether a locally finitely piecewise affine homeomorphism can be upgraded to a diffeomorphic approximation in the relevant Sobolev topology.
correct_elements: The draft correctly identifies the higher-dimensional setting n >= 3, works on open subsets of R^n, focuses on piecewise affine homeomorphisms, and asks the right qualitative question: whether such maps admit approximation by diffeomorphisms in a Sobolev topology. This does match the paper's key reduced subproblem highlighted near Proposition 1.2 and Theorem 1.3.
missing_details: The paper works with a homeomorphism f: Omega -> Delta between open subsets Omega, Delta subset R^n, not just a map Omega -> R^n with unspecified image.
The relevant notion is locally finitely piecewise affine homeomorphism, i.e. affine on each simplex of a locally finite triangulation; the local finiteness is part of the paper-faithful formulation.
The Sobolev hypotheses are not just informal: one needs f in W^{1,p}(Omega, R^n), and in the bi-Sobolev formulation tied to Conjecture 1.1 one also needs f^{-1} in W^{1,q}(Delta, R^n).
The exponents p and q, with 1 <= p, q < infinity, are missing.
The approximation is quantified: for every epsilon > 0 there should exist a diffeomorphism approximant.
The approximating maps should be diffeomorphisms g: Omega -> Delta onto the same target domain, not merely smooth injective maps into R^n.
The paper's reduction is naturally bi-Sobolev: the inverse should also approximate, namely in W^{1,q}(Delta, R^n), not only f itself in W^{1,p}(Omega, R^n).
Your draft says 'in the Sobolev norm' singular, but the paper-faithful reduced question is about the specific norm expression ||f-g||_{W^{1,p}(Omega)} + ||f^{-1}-g^{-1}||_{W^{1,q}(Delta)}.
The draft does not indicate that this is the piecewise-affine reduction of the broader Ball-Evans conjecture rather than the full conjecture itself.

The nearby Theorem 1.3 shows only approximation by smooth injective maps, so the missing issue is specifically promotion to diffeomorphisms (and, in the bi-Sobolev version, simultaneous control of inverses).
refined_question: Let n >= 3, let Omega, Delta be open subsets of R^n, and let f: Omega -> Delta be a locally finitely piecewise affine homeomorphism such that f in W^{1,p}(Omega, R^n) and f^{-1} in W^{1,q}(Delta, R^n) for some 1 <= p, q < infinity. Is it true that for every epsilon > 0 there exists a diffeomorphism g: Omega -> Delta such that ||f-g||_{W^{1,p}(Omega, R^n)} + ||f^{-1}-g^{-1}||_{W^{1,q}(Delta, R^n)} < epsilon?
justification: The draft is not aiming at the full Ball-Evans conjecture for arbitrary Sobolev homeomorphisms, but at the reduced piecewise-affine subproblem singled out in Section 1. Conjecture 1.1 gives the broader bi-Sobolev approximation goal; Proposition 1.2 isolates the corresponding piecewise-affine reduction; and Theorem 1.3 records the best nearby positive result, namely W^{1,p}-approximation of locally finitely piecewise affine homeomorphisms by smooth injective maps, showing that the missing step is precisely diffeomorphic approximation (with inverse control in the bi-Sobolev setting). Hence the refined question should add the target domain Delta, local finiteness of the affine structure, the exponents p and q, the inverse hypothesis, and the exact epsilon-quantified norm statement, while staying narrowly tied to the paper's Section 1 setup.
